title: A year after Hurricane Harvey, recovery disruption and doubts about aid distribution remained concentrated among affected residents
source_unit: KFF/Episcopal Health Foundation weighted survey of adults in 24 heavily impacted Texas Gulf Coast counties, fielded late June through late July 2018; follow-up about 10–11 months after Harvey
geography: United States; 24 Texas Gulf Coast counties containing about 94% of the population in 41 declared disaster counties

observations.period: June–July 2018, approximately one year after Hurricane Harvey

denominator.unit: Weighted adult resident survey; exact respondent count is not stated in the retained report summary

affected_share.unit: percent of residents reporting home/vehicle damage or household job, hours, or income loss

still_disrupted.unit: percent of affected residents reporting lives very or somewhat disrupted nearly one year later

financial_situation_worse.unit: percent of affected residents attributing a worse personal financial situation to Harvey

quality_of_life_worse.unit: percent of affected residents attributing worse overall quality of life to Harvey

relief_confidence.unit: percent of all 24-county residents very or somewhat confident relief money benefits those who need it most; 42% not too/not at all confident

public_input_awareness.unit: percent of all area residents aware of long-term federal funding and saying there is a public-input route; report summary also says 73% did not know enough to say

federal_or_sba_application.unit: percent of affected residents reporting an application to FEMA or SBA; among applicants 39% said approved and 42% denied

observations.method: Use the KFF/EHF weighted resident survey as a descriptive follow-up, preserving affected-resident definitions, geography, subgroup contrasts, perceived help, and relief-confidence measures; do not infer political action from confidence or awareness.
observations.uncertainty: The survey is representative of the selected 24-county region, not the United States or all Harvey residents. Affected status is self-reported; aid application, approval, satisfaction, confidence, and public-input awareness are survey reports rather than linked administrative records. The cross-section does not identify later voting, contacting, protest, exit, or causal attribution.
observations.subgroup: Affected residents, with reported contrasts by Black identity, Hispanic identity, income below 200% FPL, Golden Triangle/coastal geography, major damage, and continued displacement.
observations.counterinterpretation: A majority saying relief is reaching those most in need can coexist with substantial unmet need; confidence may reflect general preparedness judgments or information rather than realized recovery. Awareness of a public-input route is not participation.

related_sources.claim: The committed source packet records the survey source and its geography and interpretation limits.
The report provides detailed resident recovery, aid, financial, health, and relief-confidence measures.

boundary: This record closes a descriptive exposure-to-recovery-judgment arrow for a defined Texas Gulf Coast population after Harvey. It does not establish a causal effect of aid, firm survival, customer access, political participation, trust change, or general disaster legitimacy.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Existing local source-search packet and KFF/EHF report page; no survey microdata or bulk files retained
